page: Microsoft Azure E2bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is equipped with 2 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 118 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage and supports Premium Storage configurations tailored for elevated block storage throughput. The platform contains no integrated graphics processing units or hardware accelerators.

While synthetic and external benchmark metrics are currently not documented for this instance type, the hardware configuration provides distinct structural advantages. Dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute delivery without CPU contention or bursting constraints. The dense 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio targets workloads that are constrained primarily by RAM capacity rather than raw compute parallelism, enabling cost efficiency by eliminating the need to overprovision CPU cores simply to meet memory requirements.

Network connectivity features zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard virtual network configuration for external routing. The bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD functions as low-latency ephemeral storage, while persistent state is delegated to attached block storage volumes. Microsoft Azure E2bds_v6 is structurally suited for small-scale relational databases, distributed in-memory caches, ETL processing jobs, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
description: Microsoft Azure E2bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 2 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core memory allocation. Delivered through Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and offers compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for high-throughput block storage operations. The system contains no discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With dedicated compute cores and an elevated memory ratio, it delivers predictable performance for workloads that require moderate compute paired with substantial memory capacity. The local NVMe SSD provides fast temporary scratch space, while persistent data is managed via external volumes. This hardware configuration is suited for relational database engines, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, lightweight ETL data pipelines, and memory-constrained web or enterprise application backends.
